subject: Audit existing Westside palette, upgrade it in place, and build the first real new Westside homepage in Penpot
task: EXECUTE, do not stop at discussion or documentation. This task follows the existing Westside brand rather than restarting it. FIRST audit the actual current Westside Watch palette and usage from repository/source-of-truth plus the connected Penpot file. Treat the current repo palette as evidence to verify, not assumptions: First Light Gold #a2872a, Warm Gold #b79838, Morning Gold #d2bc69, Watch Night #102a43, Living Paper #faf9f5, Ink Black #252525 (explicitly NOT pure black), Olive Branch #738a5a, Living Water #5b8fa8, Harvest #b8944a, Crimson Robe #a14d57. Confirm which of these are still canonical/current before modifying anything, and inventory real usage roles (background, text, line, section accents, hero, navigation, etc.). Preserve HEX as the actual portable color values. Do not replace the brand with a generic new palette and do not force HSB/complementary-color formulas. Use the uploaded color-system article only as a methodological stimulus: inventory existing rules first, improve, test in actual contexts, then establish/upgrade tokens. Build an upgraded color system IN PLACE: retain strong brand anchors; adjust/add only where a demonstrated visual, contrast, hierarchy, accessibility or system gap exists; distinguish current/canonical values from proposed upgrades; use a pragmatic primitive -> semantic -> component token structure where Penpot supports it, while keeping HEX values explicit and human-readable. Investigate current Penpot official/free/open tooling and samples as needed, but tool study must serve this page and must not delay output. Learn why useful tools structure tokens/components/themes the way they do and adapt only useful ideas into our own architecture under the zero-incremental-paid-dependency rule. SECOND, immediately apply the upgraded color system to a REAL EDITABLE NEW WESTSIDE WATCH HOMEPAGE in the connected Penpot file. Do not make another abstract palette-only board. Create a page/board named '02 — Westside Watch Homepage v0.1' (or closest safe unique equivalent). Use the already established visual DNA Light / Line / Paper / Engraving / Architecture and editorial grammar Brick / Battlement / Flow; 5:8 remains a dominant architectural/card proportion. Reuse the 01 Lab findings if that task has completed; if it has not, do not falsely claim those findings—use the established brand sources and continue building. The homepage must visibly feel like a modern Westside Watch publication: Living Paper and non-pure Ink as the editorial ground, First Light as meaningful dawn/light rather than decorative gold everywhere, restrained section colors, 1px rules, generous editorial whitespace, Cormorant Garamond + Noto Serif TC intent, masthead/navigation, a strong opening/hero, an editorial feature/content field, and at least one architecture/brick/battlement-derived structural passage. Avoid nineteenth-century cosplay and avoid generic SaaS/card-grid aesthetics. Build desktop plus a meaningful mobile adaptation as editable Penpot objects/components. Export REAL PNG evidence from the homepage board(s), run Gemma visual verification, inspect the rendered page, automatically correct obvious hierarchy/color/spacing/brand failures, and finish only when at least one homepage PNG has image_count > 0 and visual verifier PASS. Return: (1) existing palette audit with source/current status, (2) exact current->upgraded HEX/token map and reasons for every changed value, (3) page/board/shape/component IDs and dimensions, (4) any Penpot tools/samples studied and the transferable design reasoning learned from them, (5) export evidence and Gemma verdict, (6) font/API limitations. Discussion is subordinate to execution: the acceptance target is a real editable new Westside homepage, not a plan.
